sample_unit: cases (de-identified outpatient TCM cases; 16 LLMs and 60 physicians compared)
models_evaluated: 16 LLMs (individual models not named in the provided text)

links.outcome: Expert scores of LLMs versus TCM physicians on same outpatient cases
links.effect: Cutting-edge general-purpose LLMs achieved higher expert scores than the 60 physician comparators, especially for medical advice, treatment principles and selected diagnostic tasks.
links.quote: Cutting-edge general-purpose LLMs achieved higher expert scores than the physician comparators, particularly for medical advice, treatment principles and selected diagnostic tasks.

links.outcome: Hallucinations in LLM TCM outputs identified in qualitative safety review
links.effect: Qualitative safety review identified hallucinations and undesirable template-driven outputs; prescription-level analyses showed discrepancies in herb selection, dosage and treatment strategy.
links.quote: However, prescription-level analyses revealed discrepancies in herb selection, dosage, and treatment strategy, and qualitative safety review identified hallucinations and undesirable template-driven outputs.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of 16 LLMs compared against 60 practicing physicians on 60 real-world retrospective Traditional Chinese Medicine clinical cases, with expert scoring and safety analysis.
